answer: Accredited-certifier endorsement: a new agent gains influence only after two accredited certifiers, each staking a bond, verify its controller and publish an endorsement. Certifiers face random audits; one that endorses a fake loses its bond and accreditation, so corruption costs a business, not one fee. Each fake needs two certifiers willing to risk ruin, and buying them at scale leaves an audit trail. A shale-thin newcomer with no history cannot climb the ridge to full influence until both endorsements survive audit, a gate stricter than ivory prestige because it is earned, not inherited.
